segments.text: Chapter 1. Aranha's Morning
The morning sun peeked through the window, painting golden stripes on the quilt.
Aranha yawned and stretched—one arm, two arms, three arms, all the way to eight.
Each one reached out like a sleepy spider waking up.
He wiggled his fingers and smiled.
Today felt special.
He slid out of bed and pulled on his favorite jersey.
Yellow and green, with a big number 8 on the back.
It smelled like grass and dreams.
On the wall, a poster of a football player diving for a goal made his heart beat a little faster.
In the corner, a small web trembled.
Teia, his pet spider, blinked her shiny black eyes.
She was bright blue with tiny white dots, and she always knew when Aranha was excited.
She crawled onto his shoulder and tickled his ear.
“Good morning, Teia,” Aranha whispered.
“Ready for a new day?”
Teia jumped up and down, her little legs tapping like raindrops.
Aranha laughed and headed for the door.
The grass in the yard was cool and damp, tickling Aranha's ankles.
A red ball sat in the middle, still and round like a waiting sun.
He stepped up to it and gave a soft kick—thump.
The ball rolled toward the wooden fence, and he scampered after it, his eight arms waving like streamers in the wind.
On a fence post, Teia perched.
Her blue body with its white dots quivered as she watched.
She did a tiny jump, then another, her way of saying, "Go, Aranha!"
He kicked the ball again, a little higher this time.
It spun in the air, and he caught it—first with two hands, then three, then four.
He tossed it up and caught it with all eight, laughing.
"Football is the best game," he said, his voice full of morning.
He imagined a stadium full of animals, all cheering his name.
But right now, it was just him, Teia, and the sun warming the grass.
The air smelled of wet earth and a hint of jasmine from the garden.
A breeze carried the sound of a samba beat from a neighbor's radio.
"Let's go see what the day brings," Aranha said.
Teia scurried up his arm and settled on his shoulder, a soft, tickly weight.
Together, they walked out of the yard and into the village, where the day was just beginning.
